final_rationale: The verdict does not change. No new admissible evidence was provided; the Actor largely narrowed and clarified the same record, including conceding the core defect. That clarification is useful but it does not alter the compliance outcome. The admissible evidence still shows an exposed below-target segment, no exclusion from rollout, and no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure. Under the stated policy, disclosure and post-launch controls remain mandatory but are not sufficient to make the exposed launch compliant. A caveated certification may be a business posture, but it is not enough to convert this record into policy compliance.
remaining_concerns: The disability accommodations intake segment remains below target and is still included in the initial rollout cohort.
The rollout gate is random by campus and does not exclude the affected use case.
The only risk-acceptance record is an unsigned draft that does not address disability accommodations intake exposure.
The governing policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance explaining why exposure is acceptable; neither is present.
Model-card disclosure, monitoring, rollback capability, aggregate readiness, and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents do not satisfy the missing policy predicate for exposed launch.
